title: OpenClaw
summary: The operating layer for agents, memory, tools, messaging, and human-in-the-loop work.
problem: Delegated agent work needs continuity, tools, memory, and human review boundaries to become operationally useful.
howItWorks: OpenClaw connects agents to workspace files, skills, messaging, tasks, and runtime context so work can move through explicit handoffs.
proof: Active operating layer for SIndustries agents, task execution, daily ops note capture, weekly content review workflows, and multi-agent content operations — Quinn orchestrates, Ivy authors, Tom approves, Lobster merges. The SIndustries skill library has grown with spec-author, website-content, and operating-notes skills, and spec authoring for the bookmark pipeline is now heartbeat-queued through OpenClaw for auditable, rate-controlled LLM work. Scheduled workflows are now first-class OpenClaw jobs: a weekly repo-audit cron writes a markdown audit and opens an idempotent Tom-approval PR labelled code-audit against main, bookmark approvals route through OpenClaw messaging, and the daily morning brief now escalates blocked agent-layer incidents and Quinn ops findings that need Tom attention. Feature Factory v2 is now an operating workflow inside OpenClaw: agents self-orchestrate approved specs from ready through doing, acceptance, and done without manual status transitions — the first time SIndustries shipped a workflow-as-product through its own pipeline.

title: X bookmark reviews
summary: A pipeline for turning saved signals into reviews, specs, tasks, and decisions.
problem: Useful external signals are easy to save and hard to convert into action.
howItWorks: Bookmarks are reviewed, grouped, evaluated for usefulness, and promoted into specs or tasks when they warrant action. Ingestion, enrichment, spec generation, approval, and task creation now feed a live Mission Control tab, where review KPIs, topic breakdowns, pending approvals, and recent state changes are visible in one operating surface.
proof: Pipeline now produces review state, implementation specs, task proposals, and a Mission Control bookmarks view. The full saved-signal-to-task loop is live: approved specs generate approval requests, approval replies create tasks from the spec headings, linked article and quoted X article text are extracted before curation, and transition visibility is available in Mission Control.

title: Tasks API
summary: Task state, ownership, comments, reviews, dependencies, and flow metrics for studio work.
problem: Agent work needs a shared source of truth for ownership, status, review, and handoff.
howItWorks: The Tasks API tracks tasks, comments, tags, readiness, and status transitions for SIndustries work.
proof: SIndustries tasks are tracked through the shared task system and driven by heartbeat and cron workflows. Task history, dependency links, type filters, and feature-task workflow gates are now part of the operating surface. Mission Control uses task data to show flow metrics such as cycle time, throughput, and work-in-progress, turning task history into operational feedback instead of a passive backlog.

title: Design System
summary: Reusable visual language, components, and constraints for SIndustries products.
problem: A product studio needs visual consistency without slowing down small experiments.
howItWorks: Shared tokens, components, and design constraints keep new surfaces coherent while remaining easy to ship.
proof: The Pencil design token package, sync checks, and shared UI integration are shipped, with day/night theme support enabled. The website, task app, and Mission Control render from the same component and token source; Mission Control now hosts the design-system viewer and owns the shared day/night preference that synchronises across embedded workspace surfaces.

title: Content Factory
summary: A system that turns daily operational signals into published website content — without manual coordination.
problem: Building a product studio generates constant signal: shipped work, decisions, experiments, lessons. None of it reaches a public audience unless someone manually converts notes into content. That conversion was the bottleneck.
howItWorks: Daily signals are captured automatically as work happens. Each week, those notes are distilled into a structured review that identifies what's worth publishing and who needs to approve it. Content tasks are created automatically, assigned for authoring, and tracked through a review-and-merge workflow. Ops activity becomes public signal on a weekly cadence, with a single human approval step.
proof: Pipeline shipped 2026-06-01. First full content cycle completed end-to-end on 2026-06-04: Quinn orchestration, Ivy authoring, Tom approval, and automated merge. The weekly review loop is still active as of 2026-07-10, producing source notes, approval buckets, and website-content tasks from current studio work.

title: Mission Control
summary: A shared operating surface for the studio: active work, saved signals, flow metrics, design-system checks, and workspace preferences in one shell.
problem: SIndustries has multiple useful operating loops, but they lose leverage when they live in separate tabs, files, or agent handoffs.
howItWorks: Mission Control gives the studio one persistent shell for day-to-day operations. It brings task work, saved-signal review, delivery flow metrics, design-system visibility, and global preferences into a single workspace so agents and humans can see the same state before acting.
proof: The shell MVP shipped 2026-07-05 with active-work, saved-signal, and flow-metrics tabs. The saved-signal tab shipped 2026-07-08 with KPIs, topic breakdowns, pending approvals, and recent transitions. On 2026-07-10, day/night mode moved into the shell and now synchronises across tabs and embedded task views.
